THIS MFA.CROB IN MFA.No.2211/2018 FILED UNDER ORDER 41 RULE 22 OF CPC, READ WITH SECTION 173(1) OF MC ACT, AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED:15/11/2017, PASSED IN MVC No.3698/2016, ON THE FILE OF THE VIII ADDITIONAL SMALL CAUSES JUDGE & XXXIII ACMM., MEMBER, MACT, BENGALURU, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL ALONG WITH M.F.A.CROB, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.
The insurer is in appeal challenging the finding recorded by the Tribunal that the vehicle that it had insured was involved in the accident.
It is also contended that the compensation awarded and the rate of interest is excessive.
2. The claimants, being dis-satisfied with the compensation awarded by the Tribunal have filed a cross- objection.

3. Learned counsel for the insurer contends that Ex.R-2 the Medico Legal Register of Sanjeevini Hospital indicated that the deceased was a pillion rider and the two wheeler that he was travelling hit an Indica car from behind, whereas in the claim petition it was contended that the rider of the two wheeler lost control and hit the divider and this thereby clearly indicates that a false claim was being set up.
4.
Learned counsel also contends that the rider of the motor cycle did not suffer any injuries and this also indicates that the occurrence of the accident itself was doubtful.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is not in dispute that the incident is supposed to be occurred on 15.01.2015 at 11.30 p.m of Boodihal.
The Medico Legal Register produced indicates that the claimant was brought to the hospital at about 1.30 a.m.
Thus, the fact that the deceased had suffered grievous injuries and was brought to the hospital is not in dispute.

6. As far as the argument that the entry in the Register indicates that there was a collusion between the two wheeler in which the deceased was a pillion and Indica car is concerned, the author of the Medico Legal Register was not examined to establish this contention.
The owner of the two wheeler was served and remained unrepresented.
It is also not in dispute that a chargesheet was laid against the rider of the two wheeler.

In the light of these circumstances and the adduced evidence, the Tribunal was perfectly justified in coming to the conclusion that the claimant was riding pillion and the accident occurred when the rider of the motor cycle lost control and hit a divider.

7. As far as the contention that the rider of the motor cycle was not insured and therefore, the accident was doubtful is concerned, nothing prevented the insurer from summoning the driver of the two wheeler who had in fact been chargesheeted to establish this contention.

It has to be noticed here that the claim cannot be based on assumptions and conjectures unless positive evidence is adduced by the insurer regarding the involvement of the vehicle that it had insured and the injury suffered by the pillion rider, the arguments advanced would not be of any relevance.
Therefore, the same is rejected.

8. As far as compensation is concerned, The Tribunal has thereafter proceeded to award the following sums as compensation:
 Sl. Particulars Amount  No. In (Rs.)
 1. Loss of dependency 11,43,000/-
 2. Loss to the estate 15,000/-
 3. Burial and obsequies 15,000/-
 4.

Medical expenses 1,66,000/-
 5. Loss of love and affection 1,00,000/-

In order to arrive at the loss of dependency, the Tribunal has determined the monthly income,
notionally at Rs.8,000/-.

As there is no credible evidence to ascertain the actual monthly income, it would be appropriate and prudent to adopt the monthly income determined by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, which, for the accident of the year 2015, would be Rs.9,000/-.
10. Since the deceased was aged 26 years and was self employed, 40% requires to be added to the monthly income towards future prospects, which would result in the income to be Rs.12,600/-.
If 1/2 is deducted towards personal expenses, his monthly income would be Rs.6,300/-.
11. The income of the deceased for the purposes of determining the loss of dependency would thus be Rs.6,300/-.

sentences.text: As the deceased was aged 26 years, a multiplier of '17' would have to be applied.

Consequently,
the claimants would be entitled to a sum of Rs.12,85,200/- (Rs.6,300/- x 12 x '17') towards "loss of dependency".
13.

The claimants being the father and mother, they would each be entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/-
towards "loss of consortium" i.e., in all Rs.88,000/- and they would also be entitled to a sum of Rs.33,000/- under the "conventional heads".

14. The sum awarded as medical expenses by the Tribunal, being based on documentary evidence,
does not call for modification and hence confirmed.
Since the deceased was hospitalised for about eight days, it would be appropriate to award Rs.15,000/- towards 'conveyance, food and transportation charges' to the claimants.

15. Thus, the claimants, in modification of the impugned award, would be entitled to the following sums:
 Sl. Amount  Particulars  No. (In Rs.)
 1. Loss of Dependency 12,85,200/-

2 . Loss of Consortium 88,000/-
 3. Conventional Heads 33,000/-
 4. Medical expenses 1,66,000/-
 5. Conveyance, food and  15,000/-
 transportation charges

16. Thus, the claimant would be entitled for compensation of Rs.15,87,200/- as against Rs.14,39,000/- awarded by the Tribunal, along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
17. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
18. The apportionment of compensation amount would be in terms of the Award of the Tribunal.
